title: The Black Hole
citation_title: The Black Hole: A Portable Impossible Space: Greed, Visual Rules, and the Mechanics of a Moral Trap
citation_apa_title: The Black Hole: A portable impossible space: Greed, visual rules, and the mechanics of a moral trap
description: A 30-minute analysis of the 2008 short: how a single visual rule turns office boredom into greed, danger, and an ironic trap.
abstract: Phil Sansom and Olly Williams's 2008 short The Black Hole follows an exhausted office worker who receives a sheet of paper carrying an impossible aperture. In less than three minutes, an ordinary photocopier becomes the instrument of discovery, temptation, theft, and entrapment. This article argues that the film's effectiveness depends less on its warning against greed than on the precision with which it introduces and reuses a visual rule: a flat printed circle permits passage through the surface against which it is placed. The actor's gestures, the photocopier's mechanical sounds, the blue-gray lighting, and the progression from a cup to a vending machine and then a locked safe all make that rule legible without explanation.
